review_candidates.description: Ambition has no passport. That belief is why LemFi exists. We're the financial engine for people the world wasn't built to serve, the millions who move countries to build something better and find the financial system hasn't caught up with them yet. We started with remittances: the money people send home to the people they love. Now we run multi-currency accounts, Savings, eSIMs and Credit. Because staying connected to home and building somewhere new are not two separate things. They never were. About The Role LemFi moves money across 30+ countries for people who cannot afford downtime. Our infrastructure has to be as resilient as our customers are determined, and right now we need 1 person to own that end to end. This role sits inside the core engineering team and is the single point of accountability for how we plan for failure, test for it deliberately, recover from it fast, and prove with data that we are getting better every quarter. You will work across cloud infrastructure, databases, and platform tooling to build systems that bend without breaking. If you are the kind of engineer who would rather break things in a controlled blast radius on a Tuesday afternoon than be paged at 03:00 on a Saturday, this is the job for you. What you'll build and own Own the disaster recovery programme end to end: design runbooks, run drills, close gaps, and report hard RTO/RPO numbers to the business. Build and mature a chaos engineering practice, designing experiments that surface real weaknesses before customers find them. Design and operate database monitoring across the stack so degradation, replication lag, or backup failures surface immediately, not after the fact. Define and track resilience benchmarks and SLOs that give engineering leadership a clear, honest picture of system health, not a vanity dashboard. Own backup strategy and integrity: automate, test restores regularly, and treat an untested backup as no backup at all. Use AI tooling to accelerate incident analysis, pattern detection in observability data, and runbook generation so the team moves faster on every incident. Partner with product and platform teams to embed resilience requirements early in design, so reliability is never a last-minute retrofit. Your experience 5 or more years in cloud infrastructure or site reliability engineering, with clear ownership of resilience or availability outcomes. Hands-on experience designing and executing disaster recovery plans and chaos experiments in a production cloud environment. Strong working knowledge of database operations: replication, backup, restore, monitoring, and failover across at least 1 major engine (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or similar). Comfortable with infrastructure-as-code and the tooling that keeps cloud environments observable and controllable. Experience defining SLOs, error budgets, or resilience benchmarks that the wider engineering org actually uses. Able to translate resilience data into plain language for non-technical stakeholders, because a metric nobody understands changes nothing. Bias for action when systems are degraded: you investigate, communicate clearly, and drive resolution without waiting to be told. Nice to have Experience in fintech, payments, or any regulated environment where data integrity is non-negotiable. Familiarity with multi-region active-active or active-passive architectures at scale. Contributions to chaos engineering frameworks or open-source observability tooling. Why join LemFi? Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down. Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours. Follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play. Don't feel that you're right for this role, but want to submit your interest in working for LemFi? You can join our talent community to stay in touch for future opportunities. Recruitment agencies notice LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee. AI in hiring at LemFi We use AI to cut admin, like notetakers that let interviewers focus on the conversation instead of typing. AI never makes hiring decisions. That responsibility always sits with our hiring teams. Read our AI use policy to see how we use AI and how we expect you to use it too.

review_candidates.title: Senior Cloud Security Specialist
review_candidates.description: Black Duck Software, Inc. helps organizations build secure, high-quality software, minimizing risks while maximizing speed and productivity. Black Duck, a recognized pioneer in application security, provides SAST, SCA, and DAST solutions that enable teams to quickly find and fix vulnerabilities and defects in proprietary code, open source components, and application behavior. With a combination of industry-leading tools, services, and expertise, only Black Duck helps organizations maximize security and quality in DevSecOps and throughout the software development life cycle. Job Title: Senior Cloud Security Specialist Reports to (Direct Title): Sr. Manager, Threat Intelligence Department: Cybersecurity Operations Position Summary This role secures the multi-cloud infrastructure behind Black Duck's SaaS platforms. The Senior Cloud Security Specialist is a hands-on technical contributor responsible for operating and continuously improving Black Duck's cloud security tooling ecosystem, with particular ownership of the Wiz Security Platform. The role ensures cloud assets are accurately discovered, security scans run on schedule, policies and controls are tuned to produce actionable results, and coverage gaps are investigated when Wiz or other tools do not identify expected issues. Working with engineering, platform, DevOps, and Security Operations teams, this role drives vulnerabilities and misconfigurations through remediation, automates repeatable work, and communicates cloud risk clearly to technical teams and management. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Contribute to and maintain Black Duck's cloud security baseline: standards, guardrails, and reference configurations for GCP, Azure, and AWS, written so engineering teams can apply them consistently. Design, build, and operate preventive and detective controls for SaaS workloads, including identity and access (IAM, workload identity, service accounts), network segmentation, encryption and key management, secrets handling, and logging coverage. Own the day-to-day operation, tuning, and enhancement of the Wiz Security Platform and related CNAPP capabilities: onboard cloud accounts and Kubernetes clusters, configure scanning schedules, write and refine policies and custom controls, reduce noise and false positives, and expand coverage from agentless scanning to runtime sensors. Triage cloud posture, vulnerability, identity, and exposure findings based on exploitability and business risk, then partner with resource owners to prioritize and complete remediation against established policy SLAs. Maintain accurate visibility of cloud assets, workloads, services, identities, and ownership across Black Duck's environments; identify unmanaged, unscanned, or incorrectly classified assets and close inventory and coverage gaps. Validate that Wiz and connected security platforms are producing expected results. Investigate missing findings, failed or incomplete scans, integration issues, and discrepancies between tool output and the actual cloud environment. Secure containerized and Kubernetes platforms (GKE, AKS, and EKS), including cluster hardening, RBAC, admission control and policy as code, image provenance, and runtime protection. Build security into CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code workflows through IaC scanning, image scanning, secrets detection, and policy gates so issues are identified before deployment. Develop and maintain cloud detections using audit logs, control-plane events, and CNAPP signals; confirm that required telemetry is collected, retained, and available for investigation. Support the CSIRT on cloud incidents through scoping, containment, evidence preservation, cloud forensics, remediation, and post-incident hardening. Automate security controls, enrichment, reporting, and remediation workflows using Python, Bash, cloud APIs, and infrastructure as code such as Terraform and Helm. Create and maintain dashboards, reports, and operational metrics for asset coverage, scan health, policy effectiveness, vulnerability trends, and remediation progress. Lead defined cloud security projects and contribute to complex cross-functional initiatives involving Engineering, Platform, DevOps, IT, and security technology vendors. Provide technical guidance to colleagues, participate in peer reviews, and share practical cloud security and Wiz administration best practices. Communicate cloud security risks, coverage gaps, and recommended actions to technical teams and management, supporting senior-level discussions as needed. Produce evidence and control documentation supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, customer security reviews, and other applicable compliance obligations. Keep current on cloud attack techniques, provider security changes, CNAPP capabilities, and emerging threats, and recommend systematic improvements. Required Education/Experience & Skills Experience: typically 5 or more years in information security, including at least 3 years of hands-on experience securing and monitoring production cloud environments at scale. Cloud depth: in-depth practical knowledge of at least one major provider (GCP, Azure, or AWS) and working fluency in a second, including IAM, networking, logging, asset inventory, and native security services. Production experience with GCP and Azure is a strong advantage. Wiz/CNAPP: direct hands-on experience administering Wiz in a production environment is strongly preferred. Experience should include policy development, custom controls, scan scheduling and coverage, asset discovery, finding investigation, integration troubleshooting, and platform optimization. Comparable CNAPP experience may be considered. Security operations: experience operating cloud logging, monitoring, vulnerability management, and detection platforms at scale, including validating findings and investigating gaps where expected issues are not detected. Kubernetes and containers: hands-on experience securing Kubernetes clusters and container workloads in production. Automation: strong Python and/or Bash skills for security automation and integration, with the ability to work directly with cloud provider and security platform APIs. Infrastructure as code: practical experience with Terraform, Helm, or equivalent technologies, including reviewing IaC for security issues and implementing policy controls. Compliance: familiarity with SOC 2 and ISO 27001; exposure to FedRAMP or similar frameworks is an advantage. Execution and leadership: demonstrated ability to work independently, investigate ambiguous technical issues, lead projects or workstreams, and build consensus across teams. Communication and education: strong written and verbal English and the ability to explain complex cloud security issues to technical and management audiences. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant certifications are a plus, including CKS, Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer, Microsoft Azure Security Engineer Associate, AWS Certified Security - Specialty, CCSP, CISSP, or GIAC.
